Grand Hotel Malahide Irish EBF Fillies Juvenile Race
Sheehy Motors Volkswagen Handicap

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up specialist with ten runs on similar going and a win and four places in those, though his last two runs have returned 6ths; at 22 days since last run he arrives fresh but his best chance relies on a chaotic pace he cannot control.

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Back from 65 days off with a 7lb claimer aboard, yet boasts the strongest similar-going profile in the field (12/15, 3 wins, 8 places) and finished 2nd twice at 5f-6f on Good recently — the layoff is the only real question mark.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and tongue-tie and has been consistent without winning (0-from-13 on similar going), sitting in hold-up territory with a good record at 5f Good — finishes suggest market limitations rather than ability, and trainer has gone 0/5 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old filly who has won twice on similar ground and arrives just 16 days after a 5th, held up by jockey Huggan off a 10lb claim; her last two wins came at this trip on Good/Soft, and she is one who benefits if the prominent scramble creates daylight.

runners_data.name: Headmaster
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up/tracking type pushed forward on the map due to runner congestion at the rear — his two course wins came when getting a clean run from behind, and racing out of his ideal position on fast ground at 5f (shorter than his best 6f-7f) is a clear concern.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a course-and-distance win on Good already to her name this season; David Egan's ability to find positions in traffic is the key asset, and she arrives 16 days fresh with the strongest recent 5f-Good form in the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Arugam Bay
runners_data.note: 126 days off the track is a significant flag for a 3-year-old who last ran a well-beaten 9th on her comeback — previous wins were on Good ground at 5f but the layoff and that latest run make her hard to trust in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: The only confirmed leader in the field; Colin Keane takes over and Good to Firm ground (confirmed by the going report) suits her front-running style at exactly 5f — her recent win at this trip on Good and the absence of a pace rival means she can dictate entirely on her own terms.

runners_data.name: Chicago Call
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by J P Murtagh (2/17 in last 14 days) who has been beaten at 5f-7f on Good recently and has not won since a 7f Soft performance — longer trips and softer ground appear to bring out his best, making this fast-ground 5f a potential mismatch.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Strong similar-going profile (14/15, 2 wins, 6 places) and a recent win at 5f Good; Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) aboard, trainer one from thirteen in the last 14 days, but the form trend (403136) shows enough live form to make him a key player if he avoids the prominent-pack melee.

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: Has won four of her last five at 5f but all on Tapeta/Artificial surfaces — her sim-going figures on Turf-Good are only 2/10 with zero wins, arriving 170 days absent, which makes translating her excellent standard form to today's conditions a significant leap of faith.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: An on-pace type with a 5f Good win 42 days ago; trainer has zero runners in the last 14 days (0/0 form) which offers no live angle, and he has been placed only once in eight Good-ground starts, but he is fresh off a recent course success at the same trip.

runners_data.name: Finika
runners_data.note: Only three career runs so form is thin, but showed ability with a 6f Good win last time — a genuine hold-up type whose natural rear position has been shuffled forward on the map; with STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and just three runs to judge, treat her chance with caution in this congested shape.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Ran only six days ago (quick return) and is a natural prominent runner compressed into a midfield berth by field congestion — the most likely of the redistributed trio to elbow back into a forward position given the profile, but a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 and a 2nd-last run of 8th on Good tempers enthusiasm.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with Colin Keane in the saddle, she will be allowed to stride into a natural lead from the gates on this 5f Curragh straight. The problem is behind her: Ipanema Queen, Arugam Bay, Chicago Call, Genesis, Prairie Girl, and Cuban Grey all want prominent positions, creating a six-wide scramble for the three or four berths that actually exist in the first few lengths — that congestion will produce bumping and checks between the 2f and 3f markers. Focaccia, Headmaster, and Finika are genuine prominent or hold-up types who have been pushed back on the map because the race simply cannot accommodate them at the front; in reality Focaccia is the most likely of the three to muscling into a prominent berth, while Headmaster and Finika will be forced to race from further back than ideal. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable gallop in front of a messy mid-pack brawl — strongly favours horses who can settle just off the pace and produce a smooth run through the final furlong, making prominent raiders who avoid the traffic the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosie Frith Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith breaks cleanly, is allowed to set a comfortable tempo, and the prominent pack tears itself apart in traffic behind her.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates every yard from the front on Good to Firm ground that rewards a horse able to bowl along without being pressured, and the six-runner prominent pile-up behind ensures nobody gets a clean run to her until it is too late. Front-running profile with course form is ideally suited, and the sustainable pace means she does not blow up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-runner traffic chaos resolves quickly enough for one clean-travelling raider to latch onto Rosie Frith's back and overhaul her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting two or three lengths off the leader with a clear lane benefits from the collapsed rivals around them, delivering a late surge on ground that suits quick-actioned 5f types. Ipanema Queen's course-and-distance win and David Egan's positional nous make her the most dangerous profile here, with Genesis's strong sim-going record (14/15) an additional angle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack sets a genuinely hot clip fighting for position, burning themselves out and leaving room for a late-closing hold-up runner to pick through.
scenarios.body: The Highway Rat and Gazelle d'Or are the natural beneficiaries, both carrying strong Good-ground form (10/15 and 12/15 respectively) and the ability to close from off the pace; however this shape is partially dependent on Headmaster and Finika, who are redistributed away from their ideal role and therefore less likely to generate the pace collapse that this scenario needs. Gazelle d'Or's back-to-form 2nd last time at this trip and going is the sharpest angle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If widespread interference in the prominent pack stops horses cold and an under-the-radar runner finds a gap at a big price.
scenarios.body: Prairie Girl has won four of her last five at exactly this trip and surface but her sim-going figures (2/10 on Good) are a genuine worry; Cuban Grey tracked a similar path when successful at 5f here 42 days ago. Both need chaos to deliver and this is a low-probability shape, dependent on events rather than ability.

watchPoints.text: Prominent-pack traffic explosion: Ipanema Queen, Arugam Bay, Chicago Call, Genesis, Prairie Girl, and Cuban Grey all want the same two or three berths — watch for a multi-horse check or bump between the 3f and 2f poles that could end races for several of them simultaneously.

Rosie Frith's gate break: her entire race hinges on a clean exit from the stalls — if she misses the kick even marginally, the six prominent types swamp her immediately and the entire pace map is redrawn.

Gazelle d'Or's 65-day absence: she is the most interesting hold-up angle on form, but a 65-day break for a 4-year-old filly with a 5lb claimer in the saddle means race-fitness is unproven — watch her post-race for signs of needing the run.

Prairie Girl's going suitability: her four recent wins are all on Artificial/Tapeta, and the going report confirms Good to Firm — if she tracks up travelling well early and weakens sharply, it confirms the surface is the limiting factor rather than ability or fitness.

Headmaster racing shorter than ideal: his two wins came at 6f-7f and he is a natural hold-up type now at 5f on fast ground in a field that may not generate the pace collapse he needs — any sign of being shuffled wide or checked early should be noted.

races.name: FBD Hotels And Resorts Phoenix Sprint Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: 9-year-old who is thriving in this trip-and-going range right now — two wins and three places from five runs on similar ground — and his natural prominent style fits the expected race shape perfectly without any positional conflict; W J Lee takes over.|Big Mojo|Confirmed front-runner who has earned a high style-fit in his lead role but his recent form (0,8,7,10 before a comeback win) suggests vulnerability at Group 3 level, and Tom Marquand will need to find a good rhythm to hold on; racing in role for once but the class ceiling is a concern.|Bodhi Bear|Has shown real ability when winning over 5f on Good ground, yet pushed wide in the early battle for prominent position given the crowded pace scenario — Colin Keane's supreme positional judgement is the biggest asset here, and if he secures a handy berth quickly the talent is undeniable, but a poor 18th last time at this track is a flag.|Bucanero Fuerte|All five career runs have been placed or better at 5-6f on quick ground in Spain and Ireland, and Robson De Aguiar's yard has a live runner on the day (1/5 T14), but this horse's natural instinct to race prominently means he enters a positional fight he may not fully win; front-end crowding could cost him rhythm in the early stages.|James's Delight|Clive Cox sends this 5-year-old back from a 78-day break with a strong record fresh (won on return before), but two poor efforts at this course over 6f on Good ground are a red flag, and being the horse most likely displaced from his preferred prominent slot means he may find himself further back than ideal — Dylan Browne McMonagle's tactical brain is his best hope.

races.paceDynamic: Big Mojo is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners on Good to Firm ground over 6f at the Curragh, he should be able to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead and dictate a sustainable gallop from the front. Bucanero Fuerte, Bodhi Bear, and James's Delight are all natural prominent types but the map cannot accommodate all of them in their preferred position — Bucanero Fuerte and Bodhi Bear are most likely to challenge Big Mojo for the early lead, with James's Delight the least pace-committed of the three and therefore most likely to be shuffled back. Big Gossey is the only runner who sits naturally just off the pace in a genuine prominent role, giving him a clean positional berth without fighting for space. With Big Mojo able to set an honest but unforced pace and no true hold-up horse in the field, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can sit a length or two off the leader and quicken from a smooth position through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Big Mojo Leads, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Big Mojo secures the rail and sets a controlled, honest pace with Big Gossey or Bodhi Bear travelling smoothly just off his shoulder.
scenarios.body: Big Mojo rolls along at a fair but unforced clip on the Good to Firm ground, setting it up for a prominent runner to launch from a perfect stalking position in the straight; the horse with most cover and clearest run through the final furlong profits most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If challenges from Bucanero Fuerte and Bodhi Bear force a fast early pace that burns off all rivals, leaving Big Mojo to coast home on a soft lead.
scenarios.body: Should the early scrap between prominent types prove more vigorous than expected, runners chasing them tire from two furlongs out while Big Mojo, having set a pace that suits him, lengthens again through the final furlong; a resilient front-runner's race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and James's Delight, forced wide and back, produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: James's Delight, a natural prominent horse pushed to the rear by the crowded front-end, would need everything else to fade and a clear wide passage to reel them in; his 78-day absence and soft-going blip in form makes this an against-the-run-of-play outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the five-runner field produces a falsely-slow pace with nobody willing to commit early and the race turns into a sprint from below the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over 6f at the Curragh on fast ground would favour raw speed and a big cruising-speed engine rather than a hold-up style; in a field where most want to be handy, the horse who can quicken sharpest from a standing start over the final furlong wins.

watchPoints.text: Big Mojo's price could be vulnerable if Bucanero Fuerte and Bodhi Bear both press him for the lead early, as a contested pace over 6f on Good to Firm would undermine his entire race shape.

Watch Big Gossey's draw and early positioning — if he slots in cleanly just off Big Mojo in the first furlong, his excellent recent form on similar going makes him a significant live danger throughout.

James's Delight's 78-day absence combined with two course-and-distance flops on Good ground at the Curragh means he is doing a lot of things against him simultaneously, even accounting for a strong fresh record.

Bodhi Bear's run of 18th last time out at this very course should not be dismissed lightly — if that form repeats, Colin Keane will need to recover quickly from a difficult early position to make him competitive.

The Going Report confirms Good to Firm at this slot rather than just Good — the faster ground marginally advantages horses with proven Good to Firm figures, and Bucanero Fuerte's record on Firm is patchy compared to the others.

races.name: Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Consistent 2yo from Aidan O'Brien who goes well on Good ground with two wins and multiple placings in similar conditions; prominent style sits perfectly in a pace-collapse scenario, and the 22-day break on a Whelan/O'Brien combination at Curragh gives no concerns.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR=112 with two wins from three starts on Good at 6f and Oisin Murphy booked; a forceful front-runner who sets the tempo, his prior Curragh form over this trip in this going is directly relevant and he is the likeliest pace-setter to actually clear the traffic.

runners_data.name: Folsom Blues
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 11/76 stable strike-rate is productive and Dylan Browne McMonagle rides, but Folsom Blues has been stepping back from 7-8f in softer ground and this sharper 6f Good to Firm test represents a compressed ask — likely to lead early but vulnerable to those with a more natural 6f profile.

runners_data.name: King Of Cloughan
runners_data.note: Second Joseph O'Brien runner partnered by Sheridan, showing a solid 4-run profile including a win at 6f Good and multiple placings over 6-7f; prominent style means he tracks the leaders without burning energy in the pace battle, which is exactly the position the race shape makes valuable.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Mulvany's stable hit-rate is modest (T14: 1/13) and Wesley Joyce takes the ride; form figures of 42104 show a winner at 6f Good but also wide variability, and this Group 1 company represents a significant class step — a factor to monitor if the race falls apart late.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's runner with David Egan up is a front-runner who won at 6f Good but ran 14th at 5f previously; likely to press hard for the early lead and directly battle Celeron and Sun Goddess, which risks ensuring he contributes to the pace implosion rather than surviving it.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on the Aidan O'Brien filly who has won twice at 6f on Good ground and shows all four career runs in similar going conditions; the 43-day break is the main query but O'Brien's Curragh operation handles freshness well, and Moore's tactical judgement could be decisive in a chaotic early pace.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Twomey's runner has early-speed form and naturally wants to be in the mix, not tracking from the rear — placed at the back of the map only because all prominent slots are already crowded by stronger pace claims; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.87) reflects that racing against her instincts will likely blunt her effectiveness, though she has winning 6f form on Good ground.

races.paceDynamic: Celeron, Tribeca, Sun Goddess, and Folsom Blues all want to be prominent or lead, guaranteeing a truly contested, high-tempo gallop from the outset over this 6f on Good to Firm ground. With four confirmed pace-setters colliding for the same real estate, the early stages will be fierce, and by halfway the field will be strung out and stamina reserves fully interrogated. Carry The Flag and King Of Cloughan sit in a prominent tracking role and are ideally positioned to capitalise on any leader who overcooks it, while Velozee — a natural prominent racer — has been redistributed toward the rear given the field's saturation of pace. The race shape heavily favours prominent-to-pace horses with a proven 6f stamina kick in Good to Firm, as the leaders will burn each other off and the winner is most likely to come from just behind the speed rather than from a true hold-up position. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure their preferred spot — Celeron and Sun Goddess are likeliest to actually dictate, with Tribeca and Folsom Blues likely pushed into a harder-than-ideal battle to their left and right in the early stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Celeron, Sun Goddess, Tribeca, and Folsom Blues ignite a genuine pace war that blows up the field by the 3f pole.
scenarios.body: The four-way battle for the lead creates an unsustainable gallop that sees the lead group empty inside the final furlong, handing the race to horses who tracked smoothly just off the speed. Carry The Flag and King Of Cloughan, both proven at 6f in Good to Firm and comfortable in a prominent role, are perfectly placed to sprint past the faltering leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Celeron Controls, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Celeron clears the early pace battle and establishes a solo lead at a controlled tempo, quickening clear from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy dictates on the highest-rated runner in the field, keeping the pace honest but not suicidal, denying the trackers a true wall of pace to aim at. Celeron's two wins at 6f on Good ground in this form profile suit this scenario precisely, and a controlled lead on Good to Firm gives him every chance to score.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sun Goddess Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Goddess gets a clean lead alongside Celeron and the Ryan Moore tactical intelligence means she is ridden more patiently than rivals expect.
scenarios.body: Sun Goddess's record of four runs all in similar going with two wins over this exact 6f trip on Good ground makes her well-suited, and Moore is capable of finding a length of daylight where others find none. If she outruns her rivals' early enthusiasm and sustains into the final 2f, her class and trainer form give her a strong closing case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Steal Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace detonates so violently that even the trackers are compromised, gifting a late run to Velozee or The Scallionator from further back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the race to implode spectacularly and depends on Velozee — a horse naturally inclined to race prominently rather than from behind — to genuinely settle and produce a sustained late run, which is against her grain. The Scallionator has the 6f Good form but form figures show inconsistency, and this shape asks for a perfect storm that the data does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Celeron vs Sun Goddess vs Tribeca for the early lead — if all three go head-to-head from the off, the resulting pace could be catastrophically fast and none may survive to the line.
Sun Goddess's 43-day absence is the longest in the field; watch for any signs of rustiness in the early stalls and opening furlong, as Ryan Moore will need her to travel smoothly from the break.

Velozee is a natural prominent-going horse operating out of role from the rear; if she fails to settle or makes an uncharacteristic move to recover ground, she risks compromising both her own race and those immediately ahead of her.

Good to Firm ground across all Curragh races today is consistent and confirmed — no going variance to exploit, but horses with clear form on this exact surface are at a significant evidence advantage over those who have only run on Soft or yielding.

Both Aidan O'Brien runners (Carry The Flag and Sun Goddess) share the same trainer 14-day strike rate of 7/35 — a productive yard in current form, and the presence of Ryan Moore on Sun Goddess over Ronan Whelan on Carry The Flag is a meaningful jockey booking signal worth noting.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: A seasoned hold-up specialist with 10 wins from 15 runs on similar going; at 8 years old and 12 days since last run he arrives fresh, and Ronan Whelan gives him every chance, but this pace shape asks him to make up ground from deep and the uncontested front-runner is not going to stop early enough to suit.|

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: 63 days off the track is a query for a 6-year-old returning cold, but he has legitimate placed form at 6f on good ground and McCullagh knows his way around the Curragh; his natural hold-up style is a disadvantage if the pace is controlled rather than strong, though a clear late run could see him sneak into the frame.|

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a win at 6f on good in his recent history, but his genuine hold-up style is compressed into a midfield role here given the volume of late runners — Edward Lynam has placed him well this season and the 63-day absence is a minor flag, though the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges he cannot get his favoured rearmost berth.|

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old stepping up from 5f to 6f for Daniel Murphy, and his sole win came over 5f on good — the extra furlong is unproven, but Shane Foley's experience is a significant positive and his most recent effort (9th on good) suggests he needs the extra ground to show his best.|

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: Remarkably fresh horse running just 6 days after his last start, yet his form string shows consistent 2nd and 4th finishes at 6-7f on good ground — the pattern of near-misses is consistent, W J Lee gives him a leading rider, and Good to Firm ground suits his profile; the question is whether the tight tactical shape allows him to produce his customary late effort.|

runners_data.name: Nazario
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-strong field, and his tactical position is enormously valuable on a flat Curragh track with no direct pace rival; the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges he is sometimes asked to race more prominently than naturally comfortable, but here the role suits perfectly — the sustainable tempo he can set is his greatest weapon.|

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Thomas Dowling, which is an upgrade in the saddle, and she has legitimate placed form at 6f on good ground; her natural hold-up inclination is redistributed to midfield here because of race congestion, meaning she will need more luck in running than her record suggests she normally requires.|

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite pilot who can manufacture a run from anywhere, and this 6-year-old has placed form at 5f on good going, but the step to 6f and the redistribution from his preferred rearmost position to a midfield role means he is racing at arm's length from his best tactical environment — treat STYLE_FIT flag seriously.|

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fade flag is the defining factor — form shows a recurring tendency to fail to see out the race in the closing stages, and that pattern is especially damaging in a controlled-pace scenario where the finish line comes in a strong final furlong; Gary Carroll would need a perfect trip to overcome this structural concern.|

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Carries headgear (tv) which can sharpen his early sectionals, and his best run in recent form was a 3rd at 6f on good ground; the redistribution to midfield understates his natural hold-up inclination and Chris Hayes will need to find daylight, but the going is squarely in his comfort zone if the race develops late.|

runners_data.name: Yutori
runners_data.note: Glaring concern: all five recent runs are at 7-10f on Flat/Standard surfaces, giving him just 1 run from 7 on similar going with no wins or places — stepping into a 6f Curragh handicap on good to firm ground after 177 days off the track and out of a clear comfort zone, this is a very speculative participation.|

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old with winning form at 6f on soft and good going but recent efforts have been modest — 13th and 9th in her last two 6f runs on good ground tell their own story; Wesley Joyce (3) takes a 3lb claim which helps, but she needs more than is showing.|

runners_data.name: Beat The Devil
runners_data.note: Dramatic concern: recent history shows runs at 8-18 furlongs on good and standard ground, and stepping sharply back to 6f on Good to Firm after 28 days is a significant ask — Rory Cleary cannot override a horse who has been running at completely different trips and surfaces and whose redistribution to midfield reflects a horse likely lost in this scenario.|

runners_data.name: Caislean Ni Cuan
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old for Thomas Mullins with just three career runs all at 7f on good ground — dropping to 6f on Good to Firm is an unknown, but horses for Thomas Mullins on the Curragh deserve respect, and her prominent style puts her right in the tactical sweet spot behind Nazario if she handles the faster ground and shorter trip.|

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's 5-year-old has placed form at 6f on good ground and carries the lowest weight in the field (119lbs) with a 5lb claimer in the saddle — his prominent style suits the race shape well, and the combination of low weight and a tactical position close to Nazario gives him a live each-way profile despite his low OR.|

races.paceDynamic: Nazario is the only confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, crucially, faces no direct pace rival pressing him to the early lead — he should settle into a comfortable rhythm on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh, dictating terms at a sustainable gallop rather than a suicidal clip. Behind him, Caislean Ni Cuan and Rosato are the likeliest to track prominently given their style tags, while the bulk of the field — Go Athletico, Gerrit's Gem, Lohoobb, Sovereign Cry and others — are genuine hold-up types who will be racing from further back. This race holds significantly more hold-up types than can all be deployed at the rear simultaneously; Jon Riggens, Hugo's Girl, All Hail, Nouvel Espoir, Mint Man and others are redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would like, scrambling for position in the first two furlongs. A lone front-runner setting a measured tempo on fast ground at the Curragh — a track that does reward horses who race handily — means the tactical advantage sits clearly with prominent or close-tracking profiles who can settle just behind Nazario and kick off a true pace; deep hold-up horses are fighting a structural disadvantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nazario Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Nazario bowls along uncontested and sets a genuine but sustainable pace, allowing prominent horses directly behind to travel sweetly before delivering their challenge.
scenarios.body: Nazario's unchallenged lead creates a compressed mid-race tempo that suits horses racing in second or third gear just behind him, enabling a decisive kick in the final two furlongs on the fast Curragh surface; those who track smartly and quicken cleanly hold a structural edge over deep closers who face a wall of horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Squeeze Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just hot enough that front-runners empty out, allowing genuine hold-up horses who secure a clear run to finish powerfully through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Go Athletico and Gerrit's Gem — both proven hold-up performers on good to firm — benefit most if gaps appear late and they can produce their customary late surge; Lohoobb, who has shown consistent placed form at this trip and on this going profile, could also be delivered late by W J Lee.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types scramble for midfield and create early crowding that further neutralises the closers, leaving Nazario to steal a march that nobody can overhaul.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to force Nazario off his comfortable rhythm and a chaotic midfield battle consuming the hold-up brigade's energy, the front-runner gets first run and the Curragh's flat straight fails to provide the compression late closers need; Rory Mulligan's claiming allowance becomes a live factor if Nazario is carrying less weight than his rivals can handle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Chaos Result
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches badly in the early stages with redistributed hold-up types forcing prominent runners wider or checking momentum, producing an unusually stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: An uneven tempo scrambles the usual pace-shape advantages and opens the door to a lightly-raced or freshened type like Sovereign Cry (22 days since winning over 5f on good ground) or a hold-up horse who lucks into a clean passage through the disorder; however this scenario depends on unusual race chaos and carries the lowest probability.

watchPoints.text: Nazario's early gallop sets the entire tactical shape — if he is hassled off the break by Caislean Ni Cuan or Rosato pressing forward, the pace sharpens and hold-up horses improve in value; if he leads uncontested, trackers benefit most.

Yutori and Beat The Devil are both operating well outside their established form parameters — Yutori returning from 177 days off at a sharply shorter trip on unfamiliar ground, Beat The Devil stepping from 18f to 6f — monitor their odds movements for clues about stable confidence or whether market expects them to run their race.

The 15-runner field creates early crowding risk in the first two furlongs; horses like Hugo's Girl, Jon Riggens and Nouvel Espoir — all genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield on the map — will be jostling for position and a bad draw or slow start could cost them their race before the pace even settles.

All Hail's fading tendency in the closing stages is particularly relevant if Nazario sets only a moderate gallop — a slow early tempo followed by a strong final furlong is exactly the shape that exposes her weakness; watch whether she is eased once Gary Carroll senses her fading.|

Lohoobb's 6-day turnaround is unusual and worth monitoring — if the trainer is running him back quickly it may indicate confidence in his condition on fast ground, as his recent form at 6-7f on good is consistently placed without winning.|

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Thomas Gibney who returns after 42 days off; best form on good ground (sim-going 2W4P) and handles the trip well, but needs the pace to be genuinely strong to make an impact from the back.|

runners_data.name: Final Voyage
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight at a mile who won over 10f last time on good ground, trained by JP Murtagh; 84 days off is a significant concern and the drop back to a mile from further may not be ideal for a horse who has shown hold-up tendencies.|

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 7f on good ground and was placed over 6f recently for MC Grassick; the step up to a mile is unexplored on this going, but the p headgear and prominent style suits tracking Kalir closely here.|

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style performer with placed efforts at 8f and 7f on good ground; John James Feane runner who drops back from 9f, and the form figures of 3-2 over this trip on similar ground are encouraging for a tracking role.|

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Won a 9f handicap on good ground 17 days ago and was second over 8f at the Curragh for Mrs John Harrington; the b headgear has been a positive marker, and this horse's genuine hold-up style is well-suited if any pace develops.|

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: Ageing nine-year-old without a win from 15 comparable-going runs, but showed a third at 8f on good ground recently; needs a strongly-run race to get competitive from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: Four-win handler with strong recent form (163121) including two wins at 7f on good ground; a true hold-up operator whose best chance comes if rivals race prominently and the pace is contested — the redistribution to a more forward map position reflects the crowded hold-up division rather than this horse's actual race style.|

runners_data.name: Kalir
runners_data.note: Dk Weld's three-year-old who is the lone confirmed front-runner in this field; won over 8f on good ground and has strong prominent leanings (p headgear), and uncontested control of the pace from Chris Hayes is the key asset here.|

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: KJ Condon's five-year-old with a terrific recent sequence (14321) including a win last out 24 days ago, but all wins have come over 10f+ on good ground — the step down to 8f is a genuine concern, and this horse's natural closer style is squeezed by the crowded back-of-field.|

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for Adrian McGuinness who won over 7f on good ground and has multiple placed efforts; the t headgear applied, and while this horse naturally wants to close from behind, its trip form at 7f hints it may not fully stay if used prominently here.|

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: The other McGuinness runner, wearing tp headgear, with five placed efforts from 15 comparable runs and no wins at the mile trip in recent form; a natural hold-up horse who needs genuine pace and a clean passage, and at 10 days between runs arrives with fitness.|

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: The three-year-old from Mrs John Harrington with a strong placed record (2-1-5-3) including wins over 7f; prominent style suits the map well, and although the p headgear is familiar, the step to 8f on quick ground is mildly unexplored — Keithen Kennedy claims 5lb.|

races.paceDynamic: Kalir is the confirmed front-runner here, with Chris Hayes likely to slot him onto the lead from an early stage and control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over one mile at the Curragh. With only one genuine pace-setter, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the race and means those racing prominently behind Kalir — Glory To Be, Playin Cool, and Glitter And Glory — are ideally placed to travel within themselves and pounce entering the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear: Summer Island, Marmeladova, Goal Exceeded, and No More Porter are all natural closers who will be competing for a limited number of back-of-field positions, meaning several will race out of role in a more prominent berth than they prefer. This race shape most favours prominent racers who can sit just off Kalir's controlled pace and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than hold-up horses who will need a strong gallop to generate the momentum to close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalir Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Kalir leads at a measured gallop and prominent chasers Glory To Be or Playin Cool track him throughout to collar him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kalir sets an uncontested, comfortable pace that suits horses travelling on his heels, with the race unfolding at a rhythm that never truly tests stamina or creates a meaningful gap for hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kalir Holds On To Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that Kalir himself is never headed and his rivals run into each other chasing him late.
scenarios.body: Kalir's uncontested lead from the front on fast ground means he conserves energy perfectly, and the prominent pack behind him burns more fuel trying to close than Kalir does holding the advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop collapses entirely and the hold-up horses redistributed into midfield manage to find sufficient momentum off a stop-start pace.
scenarios.body: Dark Viper, who has recent good-ground form and a genuine late-run profile, is the most plausible beneficiary, with Summer Island and Marmeladova also capable if they avoid traffic in a compressed finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Develops, True Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If secondary pace horses like Glory To Be and Playin Cool push up aggressively and force a genuinely hot tempo that blows the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would drain the prominent group and allow the furthest-back finishers to reel them in late, with No More Porter and Howyoulikethat among those to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Kalir (Chris Hayes) jumping cleanly and establishing the lead unchallenged — if he gets uncontested control of the pace from the off, the race shape tilts decisively in his favour and those around him.

Summer Island, Marmeladova, Goal Exceeded, and No More Porter will all be competing for the same limited rear positions — watch for traffic problems and shuffling for position in the back straight that could cost any of them several lengths.

Glory To Be stepping up to a mile for the first time on this going for MC Grassick — if the horse finds the extra distance beyond its comfort zone, it may drop away despite a perfect tactical position tracking the leader.

Marmeladova's record is entirely built over 10f-12f — a drop to 8f is the sharpest trip test this horse has faced, and if the pace is controlled rather than searching, the closing run may simply arrive too late over the shorter trip.

Glitter And Glory's 5lb claim for Keithen Kennedy could be influential in a tight finish if the prominent group fires together — watch whether the weight advantage translates into a length's edge in the final 100 yards.
